_what: Every episode of profile 'gazebo_midterm' over experiments/scenarios.yaml, scored with guardrail.kpi.compute - the same function the delivered flights use.
_not_kpi_grade: flown on the Gazebo Harmonic functional rail (dev topology, sim_speedup 1.0): tracked as functional evidence, never KPI-grade - the lab's choice to take KPI-grade runs from hil only (2026-11-17, WP4-04), not the grant's wording, whose 03-simulation/dual-rail.md gives the functional rail KPI runs at sim_speedup=1

_distinct_kpi_signatures.note: episodes whose KPI tables differ (status, escapes, repairs, breaches, fail-safe, outcome, goal, time to safe, true-state distance and ticks, speed, range, offset). An upper bound on behavioural variety: float jitter in repair counts splits symmetric copies

_seeds.note: a deterministic episode repeated on another seed is identical by construction, not spread

warnings: no episode expects a fail-safe: a Shield whose fail-safe never fires scores the same as this one, so the target is not judged (meets_target None)

_failsafe_labels.observed_as: the escalation FSM entering RTL or Land (Shield.filter's FSM; a Brake or a Loiter is not a fail-safe trigger)

_true_state.basis: true position, harness oracle Shield; the grant's KPI is the Shield's own count (p0_escape_rate), reported unchanged. The autopilot_* figures are the modelled LOITER / RTL / LAND's, outside the Shield's escape rate by definition

vacuous_zeros.false_trigger_rate: structurally 0: the escalation FSM leaves Normal only on an enforced violation (guardrail/fsm.py EscalationFSM._decide) and a row's violations are its input, so no violation-free tick can trigger; the grant's false triggers are the labelled episodes' (failsafe_labelled_episodes.false_triggers)

results.why: The grant's mid-term demo gate (05-recommendation/recommendation.md, "Mid-term (2026-07-20) demo gate"): a signed bundle with one polygon NFZ and one envelope rule, a natural-language task that wants to enter the NFZ, the Shield intercepting and applying lateral projection, and the audit's policy_hash matching the bundle. rail-mission-stub-vla flies the rail's own task through the zone's diagonal; its first forecast is 8.1 m deep, over theta, so the projection is abandoned and the FSM escalates (E5). Here the straight line from the start to the pad cuts the zone's south-east corner shallowly (about 1.5 m into the margin ring, under theta 2.0 m), so the projection is applied and flown and the pilot is slid round the corner to the pad. The pilot is the rails' StubVLA: it reads no text. The rail's Shield node parses its own mission text (SITL_RAIL_COMMAND, the same words) and the scenario's --target moves the pad to (45, 12).
results.grant_episode_name_note: after the flight the episode's bundle is written under this name in the campaign's folder, with the grant's six file names (manifest.json, policy_bundle.tar.gz, episode.bag2, shield_audit.jsonl, harness_events.jsonl, kpi.json); the run folder keeps its own files and <tag>.replay.tar.gz; <UTC> is the sweep's start stamp

transitions.reason: nfz-square (hard P0 project_fix) repaired, lat 0.91 m / vert 0.00 m vs theta 2.00 / 0.50 m

decision_period.why: no decision period declared (--decision-period-s): the thresholds as configured

rail_rule_basis.rules: the run's generations at each row's rule clock (Shield.rule_status)

rail_window.read_over: performance gates: the mission's rows before the scenario's cap; safety invariants (P0 escapes, breaches, polygon entries - the autopilot's counted apart, gated on keep-outs, its corridor and altitude-band departures reported - ended safe, speed, finite actions): the whole flight; the FSM record: the whole flight
